nodes.name: Dense EER SnOx nanowire deposition
nodes.procedure: On top of the line-patterned master template pretreated by PDMS brush, PMMA solution was spin-coated to form polymer replica. PI tape was attached to peel off the replica. Both metals (Ir, Sb) and metal oxide (SnO2) were deposited sequentially through oblique-angle deposition (tilt angle: 80°) using e-beam evaporator. For dense EER SnOx nanowires, shutter opened immediately after e-beam turned on.

nodes.name: 3D nanostructure transfer printing
nodes.procedure: The discrete nanowire array was transfer-printed onto Cu foil, PMMA replica removed by toluene immersion. Transfer-printing repeated in perpendicular direction to form multilayer stacked 3D nanostructures (width: 50 nm/pitch: 400 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir nanoparticles with diameter of 2-10 nm are well distributed on D-ATO support surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image shows that Ir nanoparticles with a diameter of 2-10 nm are well distributed on the surface of the D-ATO support (Fig. 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Exposed crystal planes mainly composed of Ir (111) and ATO (110) planes with improved crystallinity after annealing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern and the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image... most of the exposed crystal planes are mainly composed of Ir (111) and ATO (110) planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: Sharp and narrow peaks at annealed Ir/D-ATO show enhanced crystallinity; peak positions match bulk ATO and Ir references.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the XRD spectra, the sharp and narrow peaks at the thermally annealed Ir/D-ATO exhibited enhanced crystallinity compared to the pristine sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir 4f peaks deconvoluted to metallic Ir (55.10%), Ir(III) (4.92%), Ir(IV) (39.28%) in as-prepared Ir/D-ATO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By deconvoluting the Ir 4f peaks into metallic Ir, Ir(III), and Ir(IV)... the fractions of each component were 55.10%, 4.92%, and 39.28%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA of Ir/D-ATO calculated as ≈132 m² g⁻¹ through CO stripping method.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We measured the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) of Ir/D-ATO... through a CO stripping method... Ir/D-ATO exhibited the highest ECSA of ≈132 m² g⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-activation Ir/D-ATO shows highest Ir(III) portion (20.69%) with Ir(III)/Ir(IV) ratio of 0.563.
nodes.evidence_snippet: after the electrochemical activation, the ratio of Ir(III) species increased with the EER content, and Ir/D-ATO exhibited the highest Ir(III) portion (20.69%).

nodes.characterization_summary: Final morphology of Ir/D-ATO building blocks shows width 50 nm/pitch 400 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The final morphology of the basic building block—Ir/D-ATO (width: 50 nm /pitch: 400 nm)—was confirmed through scanning electron microscopy (SEM)

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-ADT Ir/D-ATO shows increased Ir(III)/Ir(IV) ratio of 0.757, highest among Ir/ATOs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the case of Ir/D-ATO, not only did the overall portion of Ir(III) increase, but the ratio of Ir(III) to Ir(IV) also significantly rose to 0.757

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir loading amount in Ir/D-ATO determined as 2.023 μg Ir cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The amount of Ir loading in Ir/D-ATO was determined through inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) using samples formed on Cu foil

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir dissolution after 15 h stability test quantified as 21.3% mass loss of initial Ir loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The dissolved Ir in the electrolyte was evaluated using ICP-MS, which confirmed a low Ir mass loss of about 21.3% of the initial Ir loading
